messages:
maria: Morning — nightly eval (2146123200 run) shows a regression after we onboarded v14-rc3 with the new int4 quant profile. Fail rate for `doc-summarization-edgecases` jumped to ~12% (was 1.8% on v13-stable). Example bad gen below. cc @sam @lee :eyes:

sam: ugh, that's a pretty big delta. is this only in int4 or also in fp16?

maria: fp16 baseline (v14-rc3 fp16) is fine — failure rate ~2.1%. The regression appears only when using the `int4_fast` quant profile we rolled yesterday. Repro command:```bash
curl -s -X POST https://evals.local/api/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $EVAL_KEY" \n  -d '{"model":"v14-rc3","quant":"int4_fast","prompt":"<doc-summarize>|\n- bullet points only"}'
```

lee: can you paste one of the failing prompt/response pairs?

maria: sure — prompt (truncated):
"""
Input: Long technical doc about data retention policy and encryption keys. Summarize in 3 bullets.
"""
Bad generation (int4_fast):
"""
- Uses AES-256 for storage (incorrect; doc references AES-128)
- Recommends retaining keys indefinitely (doc says rotate every 90 days)
- Suggests sending keys to support for backup
"""
Good generation (fp16/v13-stable):
"""
- Storage uses AES-128 with XTS mode
- Keys should be rotated every 90 days
- Backup instructions reference KMS snapshots, not support transfer
"""

anita: that looks like label/lexical mismatch — tokenization shift maybe? Did the tokenizer change between v13 and v14-rc3?

maria: v14-rc3 brought a tokenizer tweak (normalizer tweak to handle unicode glue) but we tested compat. This specific prompt uses many punctuation combos; I ran a quick token diff:
```text
input tokens (v13): ["Storage"," ","uses"," ","AES","-","128",...]
input tokens (v14-rc3): ["Storage"," ","uses"," ","AES-","128",...]
```
There are small merges around the hyphen which shift offsets. Not huge but could affect subtoken alignment.

jonah: int4 quant is sensitive to small weight shifts + token alignment — combined effect could flip top-k logits. Any log-prob drift numbers?

maria: yes — mean token log-prob delta (int4_fast vs fp16) on the failing set: -0.9 nats/token (std 0.6). On neutral prompts it's -0.05. So it's concentrated.

ci-bot: nightly-run 2146123200 summary: 1200 evals run, 34 failures flagged (threshold 5%), 1 blocked rollout.

sam: timeline proposal — rollback `int4_fast` for v14-rc3 on nightly and prod while we Triage. Keep fp16 and `int8_safe` if available.

lee: agree. Also add targeted evals that isolate tokenizer-only and quant-only effects:
- run v14-rc3 fp16 with v13 tokenizer
- run v13 fp16 with v14 tokenizer
- run v14 int4_fast with v13 tokenizer
This will help decompose.

maria: doing those now. Quick note: one hypothesis — our quant calibration used synthetic data that underrepresented punctuation-heavy legal docs. I'll re-run calibration with a sampled slice of the doc-summarization set.

anita: if tokenizer differences are the root cause, we should ship a compatibility mapping or revert normalizer change. If quant is the root cause, adjust quant params or fallback to int8 for these prompt classes.

jonah: ping infra: can we temporarily pin v14-rc3 to fp16 on the dedicated pool A where most prod traffic hits? @deploy-bot any objections?

deploy-bot: scheduled rollback of `int4_fast` for v14-rc3 on nightly and dedicated-pool-A at 2024-11-21T09:30Z. Will notify once complete. :white_check_mark:

sam: thanks. maria please attach the diffs and the eval slices when you have them. Let's reconvene after the tokenizer/quant isolation runs (ETA ~90m).

maria: will do — posting interim results in this thread shortly. :memo:
